newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks dragged down by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks dragged down by profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks slid below the key 10,000 barrier in volatile Tuesday trade, dragged down by continuing profit-taking which brokers said should last for two or three weeks.

The main 57-share industrial index fell 108.19 points, or 1.1 percent, to end at 9,910.18 after heavyweight counters bankers Barclays and clothing retailer Edgars dropped 200 cents each to 3,100 and 4,500 respectively.
"Industrials had a volatile session with declines overcoming gains. Profit-takers continued to push prices down and this should continue for two or three weeks," one broker said.

Also notable among the day's losers, steel window and door- maker Radar fell 150 cents to 500, horticulture firm Ariston and merchant bankers FMB dropped 100 cents each to 2,200 and 5,900 respectively while hotel chain Zimsun shed 50 cents to 400.

Sugar producer Hippo traded 25 cents down at 1,400, pork processor Colcom at 430 and engineering group Gullivers at 230 both lost 20 cents, seed manufacturer SeedCo shed 15 cents to 245 while tea and coffee producers Eastern Highlands and tyre company NTS were each 10 cents off at 140 and 550 respectively.

A handful of counters traded firmer with agriculture investor Chemco surging 700 cents to 3,500, winery Cairns rising 50 cents at 1,600, sugar refinery ZSR putting on 25 cents to 1,525 while pharmaceutical group Caps at 420 and battery manufacturer Chloride at 140 both added 10 cents.
Minings remained quiet with gold producer Ashanti falling 300 cents to 9,500 and Wankie Colliery down 50 cents to 500.
The secondary mining index lost 20.93 points to 1,070.29.
